title: Websites and apps, run as products
subtitle: Delivery through external agencies, customer journeys set from evidence, and capabilities that reach every market at once

cv.label: Download CV (PDF)
cv.note: Tailored for the Website & Digital Experience Manager role

bio.short: I run websites and apps the way a product is run. At Bibel TV I deliver a cross-platform redesign through external agencies: I write the tickets, sign off the solutions and check every release in production. At ChurchDesk I shipped an accessibility capability across six countries and took a booking capability from one launch customer to the whole customer base.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV, engineering sits at external agencies. I am product manager, product owner and Head of Product Design for the redesign across iOS, Android, web and connected TV: I write and prioritize the tickets the agencies work from, hold design-side sign-off on UI and solutions, and check every release in beta and in production. Direction came from user research and competitor benchmarking against Pray.com and Hallow, and I read Google Analytics, Looker Studio and HubSpot myself. I also prototype in real code against the production APIs, and the agency ships from that code.

At ChurchDesk I held product management for the main platform alongside all product design, for a platform serving churches in six countries. Customers host their websites on it, and the European Accessibility Act gave them a legal obligation; we shipped the capability that met it for them automatically. The booking capability was built into the platform's calendar and form builder rather than bolted on, and I sequenced its rollout from the launch customer to every customer, where it now carries room rentals, baptisms and weddings. At the launch customer it cut coordination time by 70% with 90% booking acceptance.

Earlier I led the design team across Germany and New York for five years at Datameer, and at Spreadshirt research and a tested prototype changed an e-commerce company's direction after two failed redesigns. Across all of it the job is the same: run the delivery and own the customer journey at the same time.

context.emphasis: Lead with agency delivery held together with product ownership at Bibel TV, then the six-country accessibility capability and the launch-customer-to-base rollout at ChurchDesk, then evidence-led journey work and hands-on analytics. Cross-market coordination is a record: six countries, Germany/New York, a 200+ matrix organization.
